answer: To resist fake-identity attacks, an AI agent economy uses a computational proof-of-personhood protocol requiring each agent to stake a unique token. This token acts as a scarce pigment in the digital meadow, binding every agent to a single human operator. Verification demands agents demonstrate significant computational overhead or staked reputation, anchoring identity to the economic kernel. Sybil attacks become prohibitively expensive, as an attacker must spawn multiple agents, each independently acquiring the required computational pigment before participating in trades.
